settings.headline: Percale Bedsheet Set
settings.subheadline: 300 thread count. One thread over, one under. Cotton only, and nothing blended in to cut cost.
settings.weave_label: Keep scrolling — the weave comes to you
settings.story_text_1: Percale is the plainest weave there is, which is exactly why it cannot lie. One thread over, one thread under, 300 of them to the inch. A blend hides behind a sheen; cotton has to earn its hand from the fibre up.
settings.story_text_2: Ours is long-staple cotton, combed and ring-spun, then woven tight enough to hold a crease and loose enough to breathe. It comes out of the dryer matte, not shiny. That matte is the tell.
settings.comparison_heading: Same word on the label. Different thing in the box.
settings.footer_tagline: Sleep on truth. 100% cotton, natural latex, high-GSM towels.

settings.title: Long-staple cotton
settings.text: Longer fibres mean fewer ends sticking out of the yarn, which is why the sheet gets softer instead of fuzzier.

settings.title: Combed, ring-spun yarn
settings.text: Combing pulls the short fibres out before spinning. It wastes cotton and costs more. It is also the only way to stop pilling.

settings.title: Reactive dye
settings.text: Dye bonded to the fibre rather than sitting on it, so the colour goes down the drain slowly instead of all at once.

settings.title: Sleeps cool
settings.text: Plain weave leaves air gaps. Body heat leaves instead of pooling.

settings.title: Gets better
settings.text: Each wash relaxes the yarn. The best night is somewhere around wash twenty.

settings.title: No pilling
settings.text: Combed long-staple cotton has nothing short enough to ball up.

settings.title: Honest hand
settings.text: Matte, not shiny. Sheen is usually polyester doing the talking.

settings.title: Fibre in
settings.text: Long-staple cotton graded by staple length, not by price per bale.

settings.title: Combed and spun
settings.text: Short fibres removed, yarn ring-spun single-ply at 300 TC.

settings.title: Woven
settings.text: Plain weave on rapier looms in Erode, one over, one under.

settings.title: Washed and cut
settings.text: Pre-shrunk, reactive-dyed, cut and hemmed as a set.
Machine wash cold, 30°C, with like colours. Mild detergent, no bleach, no fabric softener — softener coats the fibre and kills the breathability you paid for.
Tumble dry low, or line dry in shade. Pull the flat sheet taut while damp and you will not need an iron.
Warm iron on the reverse if you want the hotel crease. Steam is enough.
Rotate two sets. Cotton lasts longer when it gets to rest and fully dry between uses.
